hypothesis: A schema-bound GPT strategist, deterministic Research OS compiler, and approval-aware Codex dispatch packet can convert one ROI-improvement review into one falsifiable research proposal, reject unsafe or unbounded proposals, and preserve deterministic lineage for result feedback without reaching purchase or production paths.
in_scope: Canonicalize and hash valid proposals deterministically
Compile a valid strategy proposal into a Research OS proposal draft without granting approval
Define a strict versioned JSON contract for one GPT-authored ROI research hypothesis
Emit a preparation dispatch packet only when the recorded Research OS state permits preparation
Emit a result-feedback packet that preserves prompt, model, context, scope, command, and artifact hashes
Reject free-form commands, unbounded variants, threshold search, result-driven candidate changes, credentials, production paths, purchase paths, and safety-flag changes
Use injected fake GPT and Codex providers for synthetic fixture tests
lineage_hash_requirements: GPT model identifier and prompt SHA-256
null_hypothesis: The orchestration layer accepts ambiguous, unsafe, or multi-variant proposals; produces non-deterministic proposal digests; bypasses Research OS approval; reaches real data, external APIs, Codex execution, production, or BUY paths; or loses prompt, model, scope, and artifact lineage in the feedback packet.
out_of_scope: Actual Codex CLI, task, agent, or subprocess dispatch
Actual OpenAI or external AI API calls
Automatic GitHub approval comments, merges, promotion, or shadow approval
Credentials, secrets, notification endpoints, purchase APIs, and order payloads
Feature, model, calibrator, candidate, value, dashboard, production, or BUY logic changes
Horse, race, odds, payout, result, historical OOS, prospective, backtest, or ROI execution
Production deployment or formal BUY resumption
racing_mechanism: ROI research is currently slowed by manual copying between strategic review and implementation, while repeated hypothesis churn and proposal-to-code drift increase data-snooping risk. A bounded strategist contract preserves the racing hypothesis, null, target population, chronological evaluation design, rejection gate, and lineage before Codex receives work, increasing the share of independent racing signals tested without silently expanding variants or changing candidate policy.
raw_data_sources: Git-tracked Research OS contracts at base commit 385a418827fd6d1cbf9868507d53ad7a04fe172d
No external API, real race, odds, result, payout, or production data
Synthetic contract fixtures defined before implementation
rejection_gate: Any accepted request for credentials, secrets, production, purchase, notification, merge, or safety-flag changes
Any actual external API call, Codex process launch, real-data read, backtest, OOS evaluation, or ROI calculation
Any canonical digest mismatch for identical input
Any dispatch packet emitted without the required Research OS approval state
Any missing prompt, model, context, proposal, command, or result artifact hash
stop_conditions: A fixture attempts network, external API, real data, subprocess Codex execution, production, or purchase access
A proposal changes formal_buy, send_order, or stake
A proposal contains free-form shell commands or non-canonical JSON
A proposal requests more than one variant or any threshold search
GitHub approval evidence cannot be verified
target_population: Synthetic research-orchestration contract cases only; no horse, race, odds, payout, result, or production rows are included during preparation.
title: Build a schema-bound GPT-to-Codex research orchestration loop
